colour_range.text: By default each variable's colours span the 2nd to 98th percentiles of its values over the whole run (wet cells, up to 24 frames sampled), so a frame's colours mean the same as any other's. 'frame' uses the 1st–99th percentiles of the frame shown; 'fixed' takes the range typed in. The wetted fraction is always 0–1.
colour_range.title: Colour range

depth_bias.text: When zoomed out, coarse 3D tiles can hide shallow water that lies below their simplified surfaces. Water further than about 1 km from the camera is drawn slightly nearer to it (a depth bias): its position on the screen does not change.
depth_bias.title: Drawing water over 3D tiles

hazard_parameters.text: The land use (debris factor of the Defra hazard rating), the person (mass and height, and the calibration of Chen et al.) and the 'flooded if depth ≥' threshold are set under Hazard parameters in the Layers tab and kept in this browser. One land use applies to the whole domain; a land-use map is a later development. The hazard variables are derived from the depth and speed of each output frame by the viewer's server, with the same code (analysis/hazard.jl) as FloodA5Analysis and the static plots.
hazard_parameters.title: Hazard parameters

statistics.text: The maximum, first-flooding and duration maps are computed from the output frames (for a live run, from the frames the viewer's server has kept), so they are at frame resolution: a peak between two frames is missed and times are rounded to the frame interval. The model does not record per-step maxima yet. With the sub-grid (SGS) model the depth is that of the cell's lowest part, so the depth-based hazards describe the deepest part of the cell, not its average.
statistics.title: Statistics over the run

vertical_offset.text: Added to the model's heights to put them on the basemap's. Model heights are in the DEM's datum (usually mean sea level); 3D tiles and Cesium World Terrain use heights above the WGS84 ellipsoid, so the offset is about the geoid height there (between about −107 and +86 m worldwide). Each basemap has its own offset, estimated from the basemap's heights under the mesh unless given with --offset; on a flat map the lowest bed is put at the map.
vertical_offset.title: Vertical offset

wet_threshold.text: Cells with less water than 'Wet if depth ≥' are not drawn and are left out of the colour ranges and the wet-cell count. It does not change the model.
wet_threshold.title: Wet threshold

depth_velocity.definition: Water depth times the cell's speed: a common measure of the hazard of floodwater to people, vehicles and buildings.
depth_velocity.label: Depth × velocity
notes: Classes (optional): the D·V limits of the Australian combined hazard curves, 0.3, 0.6, 1.0 and 4.0 m²/s (AIDR Guideline 7-3, Table 2). The full H1–H6 classes also limit depth and velocity: see Hazard class (ARR).
depth_velocity.viewer: Derived by the viewer's server from each frame's depth and speed.

elevation.definition: Ground elevation of the cell, sampled from the DEM at pixel centres (since 0.8.0), in the DEM's vertical datum.
elevation.label: Bed elevation
elevation.viewer: Drawn as the bed surface (on by default on the flat basemaps) with its own palette, range and opacity.

flood_duration.definition: Time during which the cell's depth is at or above the 'flooded if depth ≥' threshold: each output frame counts for the interval between the midpoints to its neighbours.
flood_duration.label: Duration of flooding

hazard_class_arr.definition: Combined flood hazard curves of Australian Rainfall and Runoff: the lowest class whose limits on D·V, depth and velocity all hold. H1 (D·V ≤ 0.3 m²/s, d ≤ 0.3 m, v ≤ 2 m/s) generally safe; H2 (0.6, 0.5, 2) unsafe for small vehicles; H3 (0.6, 1.2, 2) unsafe for vehicles, children and the elderly; H4 (1.0, 2.0, 2) unsafe for vehicles and people; H5 (4.0, 4.0, 4.0) also buildings vulnerable to structural damage; H6 all building types vulnerable to failure.
hazard_class_arr.label: Hazard class (ARR H1–H6)
references: AIDR (2017). Flood Hazard, Australian Disaster Resilience Handbook 7, Guideline 7-3, Tables 1 and 2 (after Smith et al. 2014).
Smith, G. P., Davey, E. K., Cox, R. J. (2014). Flood hazard. WRL Technical Report 2014/07, UNSW Water Research Laboratory.

hazard_degree.definition: Hazard to a person standing in the flow, HD = min(1, v / Uc), from 0 (still) to 1 (the person is toppled): v the speed, Uc the incipient velocity for toppling of a person of the given mass and height in water of depth d (Chen, Xia, Falconer & Guo 2019, eq. 10 and 14).
hazard_degree.label: Hazard degree (Chen et al.)
notes: Uc = α (d/hp)^β √( mp/(ρ d²) (γ cosθ + sinθ) − [a1 (d/hp)² + b1 d/hp] (a2 mp + b2) (γ cosθ/(d hp) + sinθ/d²) ), with body mass mp and height hp (Hazard parameters: adult 75.1 kg, 1.77 m; child 25.5 kg, 1.26 m; or your own), tilt θ = 75°, α = 3.064, β = 0.303 (the paper's recommended calibration), a1 = 0.735, b1 = 0.265, a2 = 1.015e-3 m³/kg, b2 = −4.927e-3 m³, γ = 10, ρ = 1000 kg/m³.

Only toppling (moment instability) is modelled, not sliding; buoyancy is included. Water as deep as the person (d ≥ hp) gives HD = 1. The curves lie above some urban data of low depth and high velocity (Russo et al. 2013; Martínez-Gomariz et al. 2016): in shallow fast flow the hazard may be underestimated.
references: Chen, Q., Xia, J., Falconer, R. A., Guo, P. (2019). Further improvement in a criterion for human stability in floodwaters. J. Flood Risk Management 12(3), e12486. doi:10.1111/jfr3.12486
Xia, J., Falconer, R. A., Wang, Y., Xiao, X. (2014). New criterion for the stability of a human body in floodwaters. J. Hydraulic Research 52(1), 93–104.

hazard_rating.definition: Flood hazard rating HR = d (v + 0.5) + DF of Defra/Environment Agency R&D FD2321 (Flood Risks to People): d the depth (m), v the speed (m/s), DF a debris factor of 0, 0.5 or 1 by depth, velocity and land use.
hazard_rating.label: Hazard rating (Defra)
notes: Debris factor: one land use for the whole run (Hazard parameters). The default is FD2320's precautionary factor for any land use (0.5 up to 0.25 m depth, 1 above); pasture/arable, woodland and urban follow FD2321/TR1 Table 3.1 (rows: up to 0.25 m; 0.25–0.75 m; over 0.75 m and/or over 2 m/s). A land-use raster sampled onto the mesh is a later development.

Classes (FD2320/TR2 Table 13.1, EA/HR Wallingford supplementary note, May 2008): below 0.75 low hazard (caution); 0.75–1.25 danger for some (children, the elderly, the infirm); 1.25–2.0 danger for most (the general public); above 2.0 danger for all (including the emergency services). FD2321/TR1 put the last threshold at 2.5. The breaks can be changed.
With DF > 0 even shallow water has HR ≥ DF: the method is precautionary.
references: HR Wallingford, FHRC Middlesex University, RPA (2006). Flood Risks to People Phase 2, FD2321/TR1 (methodology) and TR2 (guidance). Defra/Environment Agency.

Surendran, S., Gibbs, G., Wade, S., Udale-Clarke, H. (2008). Supplementary note on flood hazard ratings and thresholds for development planning and control purpose. Environment Agency / HR Wallingford.

level.definition: Elevation of the water surface: depth datum + water depth, in the DEM's vertical datum.
level.label: Water level
level.viewer: Derived in the viewer from the depth and each cell's datum. The surface is drawn at this level plus the vertical offset.

max_hazard.definition: The largest D·V, hazard rating, ARR hazard class or hazard degree of each cell over the run's output frames, each with the current hazard parameters.
max_hazard.label: Maximum hazard

max_velocity.definition: The largest speed of each cell over the run's output frames.
max_velocity.label: Maximum speed

max_water_depth.definition: The largest water depth of each cell over the run's output frames.
max_water_depth.label: Maximum depth
max_water_depth.viewer: With any statistic shown, the time slider and playback are off; the water surface is drawn at its maximum depth over the run (cells never flooded are left out).

saturation.definition: Fraction of the cell's plan area that is under water, from 0 to 1.
saturation.label: Wetted fraction
notes: Sub-grid (SGS) model: from the cell's elevation-area table at the current water level.
Other models: 1 where the depth exceeds 0.1 mm, else 0.

time_first_flooded.definition: Simulation time of the first output frame at which the cell's depth reaches the 'flooded if depth ≥' threshold (Hazard parameters, default 0.1 m). Cells never flooded have none.
time_first_flooded.label: Time of first flooding

time_max_water_depth.definition: Simulation time of the output frame at which the cell's depth is largest (the first such frame). Cells never wet have none.
time_max_water_depth.label: Time of maximum depth

velocity.definition: Magnitude of the depth-averaged velocity at the cell centre: the unit discharge vector reconstructed from the fluxes through the cell's faces (a least-squares fit), divided by the depth.
velocity.label: Speed
notes: Diagnostic (the model advances face fluxes, not cell velocities).
Zero where the depth is below 1 cm.
Components: vel_u (east) and vel_v (north) in the output.

water_depth.definition: Depth of water in the cell, measured from the cell's depth datum: the cell elevation, or for the sub-grid (SGS) model the lowest sub-grid elevation in the cell.
water_depth.label: Water depth
notes: Diagnostic: the model's state is the stored volume per cell (also in the output, 'volume', m³); depth is derived from it.
With SGS the cell can be partly wet: the depth is that of its lowest part, not a cell average (see Wetted fraction).
water_depth.viewer: Cells shallower than the 'Wet if depth ≥' threshold are not drawn.
